summary: Templates that evaluate to None are no longer converted to an empty string; return "" explicitly in the else branch, though since 2.19.1 string module options accept None as empty string.
questions: Why is my set_fact value None instead of an empty string?
How do I make a Jinja if without else return an empty string?
Do string module options accept None in ansible-core 2.19.1?

answer_card.title: Templates can now evaluate to None
answer_card.answer_md:
Previously a template evaluating to `None` became an empty string. Now it can be the actual value `None`:

```yaml
- set_fact:
    value_none: |-
      {% if foo is defined %}foo is defined{% endif %}
```

If `foo` is undefined, `value_none` is `None`. Return an empty string explicitly:

```yaml
- set_fact:
    value_none: |-
      {% if foo is defined %}foo is defined{% else %}{{ "" }}{% endif %}
```

This is backward compatible. Since ansible-core 2.19.1, string-type module options accept `None` and convert it to an empty string, so most roles won't need changes for this.
